title: A review event record
description: One recorded human judgement about one edge. States what was affirmed; who affirmed it, when, and by what authority are supplied by the commit that introduces this record (ADR-0009).

id.description: An absolute IRI minted at serialization time. Opaque: its parts are never split back out, because a part may itself contain the separator (ADR-0007).

seg:from.description: An absolute IRI minted at serialization time. Opaque: its parts are never split back out, because a part may itself contain the separator (ADR-0007).

seg:to.description: An absolute IRI minted at serialization time. Opaque: its parts are never split back out, because a part may itself contain the separator (ADR-0007).

seg:relation.description: The kind of the edge that was affirmed.

seg:fromNodeHash.description: Optional. An event states each endpoint's hashes through its content anchors; an event recorded earlier also carries the composite node hash the edge hash folds. Absent or a valid digest, never anything else.

seg:toNodeHash.description: Optional. An event states each endpoint's hashes through its content anchors; an event recorded earlier also carries the composite node hash the edge hash folds. Absent or a valid digest, never anything else.

seg:fromContentAnchors.description: Every named content hash the source endpoint carried at judgement, each paired with the anchor it was found at (SEG-SREQ-127) — the record an event binds, and the one a per-hash comparison reads.

seg:toContentAnchors.description: Every named content hash the target endpoint carried at judgement, each paired with the anchor it was found at (SEG-SREQ-127) — the record an event binds, and the one a per-hash comparison reads.

seg:affirmedAt.description: The source revision of each endpoint at the moment of review. Its two keys are named apart from the endpoint fields above because a term is defined once for the whole context: reusing seg:from here would give a revision string the endpoint term's definition, and a processor would read it as an identifier.

seg:fromRevision.description: The source revision an endpoint stood at when the judgement was made. Nothing else correlates a source revision to the moment someone accepted it, so it is captured here or lost (SEG-SREQ-025).

seg:toRevision.description: The source revision an endpoint stood at when the judgement was made. Nothing else correlates a source revision to the moment someone accepted it, so it is captured here or lost (SEG-SREQ-025).

seg:affirmingRole.description: The role in which the affirmation was made (SEG-SREQ-049). Required, and deliberately a free string with no enum: role validation is a process concern enforced by organisational policy, not by the schema. The CamelCase spellings (RequirementsEngineer, SoftwareEngineer, TestEngineer, FunctionalSafetyManager) are documented convention, not constraint. Empty alone is refused — an empty role would satisfy the field while recording nothing.

seg:reason.description: The justification exactly as supplied (SEG-SREQ-028). No minimum length: a thin justification is the operator's to give and a reader's to judge.

sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest, lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters. SHA-256 is fixed for the whole graph, so the digest needs no algorithm beside it (ADR-0005).

contentAnchors.description: Every named content hash one endpoint carried at judgement, keyed by hash name, each paired with the source location it was found at under the name's own 'Source' suffix — the same pairing rule a node record's own entry uses. Field names are open: which names an endpoint carries depends on its kind, so pairing is checked when a review event is read back, not by this schema.
